condition: Circumferential full-thickness burn of the forearm and hand
permutationLabel: Circumferential full-thickness limb burn with distal ischaemia (6 % TBSA)
summary: 45-year-old man, 90 kg, burning cooking oil 5 h ago: circumferential full-thickness burn of the right forearm and hand (6 % TBSA); hand cool, capillary refill 4 s, weak oximetry trace, pain on passive finger extension.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Burn to right forearm and hand from hot oil
inputs.hpi: Pan of cooking oil caught fire 5 hours ago; the burning oil ran down his right forearm and hand. Increasing tightness and numbness of the fingers over the last hour.

exam.general: HR 104, BP 142/86, RR 18, SpO2 98%. Weight 90 kg.
exam.skin: Right forearm and hand: circumferential full-thickness burn (white, leathery, insensate eschar) from elbow to fingers, 6% TBSA. Hand cool and pale, capillary refill 4 s in the fingers, weak pulse-oximetry trace on the index finger, severe pain on passive finger extension, tense forearm.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Circumferential full-thickness burn of right forearm and hand with distal ischaemia
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Circumferential full-thickness burn of the right forearm and hand (6% TBSA) with signs of distal ischaemia/compartment compromise — escharotomy now; elevation; burns centre (hand, circumferential, full thickness).

mustInclude.knownGapNote: ICD T23.301A matches no pane-engine protocol (burn protocols registered for T31.3+ and T30.0/T14.0 only; no T20–T25 site codes) and the PANE top diagnosis is below 0.20, so neither the Plan tab nor the Assessment management panel produces anything; only generic clinical prompts are shown.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Map T20–T25 site burn codes; add circumferential full-thickness → escharotomy and hand → burns referral to the burn protocols regardless of TBSA.

guideline.name: ATLS 10th edition — thermal injuries
guideline.section: Chapter 9: stop the burning process; early airway control for inhalation injury (hoarseness, stridor, carbonaceous sputum, singed facial hair, enclosed-space fire); 100% oxygen and carboxyhaemoglobin for suspected CO; TBSA by rule of nines (adults) or Lund–Browder (children); fluid resuscitation titrated to urine output (adult 0.5 mL/kg/h, child ≤30 kg 1 mL/kg/h, high-voltage electrical injury with pigmented urine 1–1.5 mL/kg/h); children also need maintenance glucose-containing fluid; escharotomy for circumferential full-thickness burns; chemical burns — remove agent and irrigate with copious water; electrical — ECG and cardiac monitoring, rhabdomyolysis, compartment syndrome
guideline.citation: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. ATLS Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: ACS; 2018. Chapter 9. (Lund–Browder chart: Lund CC, Browder NC. The estimation of areas of burns. Surg Gynecol Obstet. 1944;79:352–8.)

guideline.name: ISBI Practice Guidelines for Burn Care
guideline.section: Initial assessment and resuscitation (TBSA estimation, fluid resuscitation guided by urine output, avoid over-resuscitation), inhalation injury, escharotomy, chemical and electrical injury
guideline.citation: ISBI Practice Guidelines Committee. ISBI Practice Guidelines for Burn Care. Burns. 2016;42:953–1021.

guideline.name: American Burn Association — burn centre referral criteria
guideline.section: Refer: partial-thickness burns >10% TBSA; burns involving face, hands, feet, genitalia, perineum or major joints; full-thickness burns in any age group; electrical burns (including lightning); chemical burns; inhalation injury; burns with pre-existing medical disorders or concomitant trauma; burned children in hospitals without qualified personnel; patients needing special social or rehabilitative support (including suspected abuse). (2022 ABA update to be checked)
guideline.citation: American Burn Association / American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. Guidelines for the operation of burn centers — burn center referral criteria. In: Resources for Optimal Care of the Injured Patient. Chicago: ACS; 2006.

guideline.name: National Network for Burn Care (British Burn Association) — National Burn Care Referral Guidance
guideline.section: Referral to a specialised burn service by size (children and adults, partial thickness or more), all full-thickness and circumferential burns, special areas (face, hands, feet, genitalia, perineum, major joints), chemical, electrical, friction and cold injuries, inhalation injury, suspected non-accidental injury, and burns not healed in 2 weeks (thresholds to be checked against the source)
guideline.citation: National Network for Burn Care. National Burn Care Referral Guidance. Version 1. London: NNBC; 2012.

rationale: Permutation: small TBSA but limb-threatening. Circumferential full-thickness burns with distal compromise need escharotomy; hands are a special area and any full-thickness burn meets referral criteria. Tests that a small TBSA does not hide urgency.
